sources.title: CMS State Operations Manual, Appendix C - Survey Procedures and Interpretive Guidelines for Laboratories and Laboratory Services
sources.scope: Fetched research provenance: cover Rev. 236 issued 2026-01-23; cited sections Rev. 233 issued/effective/implementation 2025-09-12. D5203 (PDF p124), D5301-D5309 (pp134-137), D5311-D5313 (pp137-140), D5391 (pp141-142). Retrieved PDF SHA-256 b6937df6f41c22541e55094f5345912289e3406e1fea6e0a4f28b86bb7566f66.
supported_claims: D5203 / 493.1232 addresses identification through receipt, accessioning, and subsequent phases.
D5301-D5305 / 493.1241(a),(c) addresses requests and requisition information; this scenario implements only a synthetic administrative subset.
D5309 / 493.1241(e) addresses accurate transcription from requisitions into a record system or LIS.
D5311-D5313 / 493.1242(a),(b) addresses written labeling/handling procedures and documenting receipt date and time.
D5391 / 493.1249(a) addresses monitoring and correction of preanalytic-system problems.
sources.limitations: Not a complete requisition or regulatory analysis. Synthetic subject tokens are not actual identification. Provider authorization, specimen suitability/acceptance/rejection, testing, and results are outside this workflow. Token, field, cardinality, time-selection, queue, and SLA rules are invented policy, not CMS mandates.

sources.title: Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA)
sources.scope: Fetched HTML overview: CLIA program scope and test-complexity context.
supported_claims: CMS describes the scope of human laboratory testing covered by the CLIA program.
CMS distinguishes requirements according to test-method complexity.
sources.limitations: Overview context only; not evidence for an accession algorithm, queue SLA, certification, or this report establishing compliance.

sources.title: Laboratory quality management system: handbook - publication overview
supported_claims: The overview includes administrative stakeholders in laboratory quality management.
sources.limitations: No unexamined handbook chapter, ISO requirement, specimen rule, or accreditation claim is inferred. The mock procedure is not clinical laboratory operation.
